summary: For each of the 5 increments the pure-helper unit test already exists (web commonTest + android src/test, both verified passing patterns). This slice adds the two missing test layers: integration tests that drive the real ViewModel/repository path through a fake data source (web) or mockk repo (android), and UI tests that render the actual composable and assert rendered text/interaction (desktop runDesktopComposeUiTest, android Robolectric createAndroidComposeRule). Web Wasm has no compose-ui-test dependency, so web-side UI coverage is delivered by desktop JVM compose tests (same commonMain composables) plus the existing hermetic Playwright visual harness; this is called out honestly rather than faked.

risks: 1) Several target composables are private (ChecklistSections, ChainIntegrityPanel, ActivityRow, ProfileBadge, the Special Hours editor section). UI render tests need them made internal or wrapped in a small @VisibleForTesting render shim; this is a source touch to non-test files and must stay behavior-neutral. 2) FakeAuntieDataSource relies on the allKinStream() default (empty) - adding the override is required for the web kin-join integration test and must not break other VM tests constructing the fake. 3) web Wasm cannot run compose-ui-test in-process; desktop-jvm compose tests cover the shared commonMain composables, but a wasm-only rendering regression is only caught by the Playwright visual harness, not a unit-scope test (documented, not hidden). 4) Robolectric AuntieOSTheme + ComponentActivity render may pull Firebase/Application singletons (AdminDataViewModel default repo = AuntieOSApp.instance.repository); UI tests must inject fakes and gate Sentry init on Build.FINGERPRINT 'robolectric' per the Robolectric-Sentry-gate memory. 5) seqHashLabel android uses Long? vs web Int? - keep fixtures typed per platform.
